messages:
claire: Dropping an alternate take: slice-based envelope derivation for lighter KMS load. We talked about this in the previous thread but wanted to capture specifics. Proposal summary: weights split into fixed slices (8MB default). Each slice key is derived from a host-local DEK via HKDF(master_dek, info=slice-id). The master_dek is encrypted by KMS and stored as wrap_ciphertext in sidecar manifest. On host startup we attempt to load cached wrap_ciphertext from cluster cache (INF-1702). If not present, we call KMS.Decrypt once to get master_dek in memory. Then slices are decrypted lazily as accessed. This avoids N KMS calls per slice.
mike: quick nit: HKDF inputs should include model_id and slice_id to avoid cross-model reuse. Also include wrap_key_kid as salt.
sanjay: agree. Also add a per-slice AEAD tag and chunk-level checksum to guard against bitflip or tampering when reading from object store. We should treat tag failures as fatal for that slice and fetch from origin as fallback.
lena: operationally we need to define what constitutes a "hotset" of slices for pre-decrypt: prefix vs profile-based hotset. Suggest a default "prefix 3" for chat models and a runtime opt-in profile generated by the warmup evaller for larger models.
claire: we should avoid changing safetensors layout. Everything lives in sidecar manifest: {slice_size, slice_count, wrap_ciphertext, wrap_kid, hotset_bitmap, slice_checksums}. Loader implements state machine: INIT->WRAP_LOADED->HOT_DECRYPTING->HOT_READY->FULL_DECRYPTING->FULL_READY. Each transition annotated with metrics.
mike: good idea to have metrics per state. Also add a guard: if decryption CPU > threshold we can pause pre-decrypt and continue streaming.
sanjay: edgecase: partial out-of-order slice arrivals due to CDN. manifest should include per-slice byte ranges and object URLs. Loader will fetch per-slice from origin if CDN returns 404 or bad tag.
lena: security: wrapped_master cache must be access-controlled. cluster cache must not expose plaintext. It stores KMS ciphertext only. Hosts request local unwrap via KMS.Decrypt. For cloud KMS that supports conditional IAM, bind to host identity.
claire: agreed. Also include plan to add unit/integ tests: simulate corrupt slice, missing slice, expired wrap_ciphertext, and ensure fallback to cold decrypt path.
bot-ops: INF-1702 assigned to infra-team. ETA: 2w.
mike: perf note: in our sim, decrypting hotset of 3 slices took 110ms CPU and saved ~340ms on first token in our benchmark. we should add multi-tenant stress tests to understand KMS pressure.
sanjay: final note: backwards compat loaders accept classic safetensors with no sidecar by falling back to whole-file decrypt. New manifests opt into slice-decrypt features.
lena: sounds good. can you include an example manifest snippet in RFC?
claire: yes. I'll post RFC draft in docs later today. thanks everyone.
